input.quote: This is IBM's entire obligation to Customer with regard to any claim of infringement.
input.rationale: Section 8.1 gives an IBM IP indemnity for Materials and Base Components with usual exclusions and procure/modify/replace/credit remedies, which meets the fallback for IP only. However, the preferred position's other heads are absent: there is no IBM indemnity for its breach of applicable law, for unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer data caused by IBM, or for IBM's gross negligence or wilful misconduct (and Section 9.1(c)(1)-(2) expressly excludes third-party claims and data loss outside 8.1). Conversely, Customer's indemnity in Section 8.2(a)(3) is materially broader than the playbook allows, covering any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" - effectively a one-way Customer indemnity for IBM's own Services (a walk-away item, only partly mitigated by the relief in 8.2(c)). We therefore added the missing IBM indemnity heads inside Section 8.1 (so they benefit from the uncapped treatment in Section 9.1(a) and the existing notice/control/cooperation procedure) and narrowed our reverse indemnity to Customer's breach of law or of this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Extend IBM's indemnity beyond IP to breach of law, IBM-caused data breach and wilful misconduct/gross negligence, and narrow Customer's Services Recipient indemnity
proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM's indemnity currently covers only IP infringement, so we added the standard heads for IBM's breach of law, IBM-caused unauthorised access to our data, and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct, and we narrowed our own indemnity so we do not underwrite third-party claims arising from IBM's own Services. If helpful, we can accept the additional IBM heads being subject to a super-cap of 3x annual charges.

ops.text: In addition to the foregoing, IBM will defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer, its Enterprise and their respective employees, officers, agents and directors from and against any third party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) IBM's breach of applicable law; (ii) any unauthorised access to, or use or disclosure of, Customer's Content or other Customer data caused by IBM, its Affiliates or Subcontractors; or (iii) IBM's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The notice, control and cooperation provisions of Subsections 8.1(a) and 8.1(b) apply to claims under this paragraph, and the exclusions and remedies limitations set out above (including the statement that Section 8.1 is IBM's entire obligation) apply only to claims of infringement.
